extracted.intended_audience: nursing educators, clinicians, and researchers who appraise evidence and develop or teach recommendations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on using the Critical Appraisal Skills Programme (CASP) check-lists alongside the GRADE approach to make transparent, GRADE-like assessments of bodies of evidence and to critique individual randomized controlled trials, with attention to applicability in nursing education and practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate CASP checklist items into GRADE
rubrics_metrics.description: All of the items from the CASP check-list can be incorporated into GRADE which might allow for wider use of its principles in nursing education and practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper argues CASP items map into GRADE constructs and that using them together could permit teaching and use of GRADE via CASP tools; minor modifications to CASP usage are required to complete outcome-level assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome-level assessment – consistency of results
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcome-level assessment should include the consistency of the results (i.e. heterogeneity) across studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author notes that additions are required to CASP to complete outcome-level assessment, specifically assessing consistency; more detail on different types of inconsistency (heterogeneity) would be useful for GRADE-like evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome-level assessment – possible publication bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess possible publication bias at the outcome level when forming a GRADE-like assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication bias is identified as a necessary addition when using CASP to perform outcome-level GRADE assessments and should be explicitly evaluated as part of the body-of-evidence appraisal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of benefits versus harms and costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide details on the extent to which the benefits are worth any harms and costs when making recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper recommends including more detailed evaluation of benefits relative to harms and costs as part of the outcome-level / decision-making assessment to mirror GRADE's Evidence to Decision considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use CASP RCT checklist to assess body of evidence and individual studies
rubrics_metrics.description: The CASP Randomised Controlled Trial check-list can be used, with minor modifications, to undertake GRADE-like assessments of the body of evidence and to critique individual studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical implication: modify how CASP is applied (add outcome-level items noted above) so the same tool can be used both for critiquing trials and for forming transparent, GRADE-like judgments about the overall evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency in moving from evidence to recommendations (GRADE principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a clearly defined, transparent process to turn evidence into recommendations, as per the GRADE Working Group guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The GRADE guidance is widely used to increase transparency; mapping CASP items onto GRADE aims to retain this transparent evidence-to-recommendation process while using tools familiar in education/practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to the GRADE Working Group's criteria for using the approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the adapted approach is consistent with the Group's Criteria for determining whether the GRADE approach was used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper states the proposed CASP-to-GRADE adaptation is consistent with the Group's Criteria; practitioners should check alignment with those criteria when claiming GRADE-like assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for nursing education and transfer to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the appraisal tool/approach is teachable in nursing education and transferable to clinical practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The conclusion emphasizes that minor modification of CASP would allow GRADE to be taught and used in nursing education and transferred to practice—so usability and pedagogical suitability are evaluation criteria.
